conditions.label: Intestinal obstruction
conditions.note: Adhesive small-bowel obstruction; laparotomy with release of a single band, no resection

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
INDICATION: small-bowel obstruction on radiographs, worsening hemodynamics.
FINDINGS: Multiple dilated fluid-filled small-bowel loops with a transition point in the right lower quadrant; collapsed distal ileum and colon. No free intraperitoneal air. Bowel wall enhancement preserved. Small volume of free fluid between loops. Infrarenal aortic aneurysm without periaortic stranding. Postsurgical changes of appendectomy and cholecystectomy.
reports.conclusion: Small-bowel obstruction with a right lower quadrant transition point, likely adhesive. No free air.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Arrival 02/14/2025 06:40

CC: severe crampy abdominal pain x 12 h with vomiting, no flatus or stool.

HPI: 72 y/o man with HTN, hyperlipidemia, CAD, GCA on chronic prednisone, BPH, remote appendectomy and cholecystectomy. Past history also includes ischemic colitis (2023) and cholesterol embolization (2024). Pain began overnight, cramping, severe. Vomited several times. Has not passed gas or had a bowel movement since onset.

Meds: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, prednisone 10, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA.

Vitals: HR 110, BP 100/60, T 38.3 C (101 F).
Exam: abdomen distended and tympanic, high-pitched hyperactive bowel sounds throughout. 

Labs: WBC 18.0, Hb 13.2, platelets 250, lactate 4.5, creatinine 1.2, electrolytes normal.
Abdominal radiograph: dilated small-bowel loops with air-fluid levels, no free air under the diaphragm.

Course in ED: NG tube, IV crystalloid. Over the following hour heart rate rose and pressure fell despite fluids. CT obtained urgently (see report). General surgery consulted at bedside; taken to the OR.

Dx: small-bowel obstruction with clinical deterioration.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 02/14/2025  Discharge 02/20/2025
Service: general surgery

Diagnosis: adhesive small-bowel obstruction.
Procedure 02/14/2025: exploratory laparotomy, lysis of a single adhesive band in the right lower quadrant. Bowel congested at the band, pinked up and was viable after release; no resection.

Course: stress-dose hydrocortisone around surgery given chronic prednisone, then back to prednisone 10 mg. NG removed day 2. Diet advanced from day 3, bowel function returned. Lactate normalized post-op. Lisinopril and amlodipine held while pressures were soft, resumed on day 4. Incision clean.

Discharge meds: unchanged home list - aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, prednisone 10, tamsulosin 0.4.
NKDA.
Follow-up: surgery clinic 2 weeks for staples; PCP 1-2 weeks. No lifting over 10 lb for 6 weeks.

General Surgery

EXAM: CT angiography abdomen and pelvis.
FINDINGS: Infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm measuring 5.5 cm maximal diameter (4.9 cm by ultrasound 08/2024). Infrarenal neck length and angulation suitable for endovascular repair. Common iliac arteries of normal caliber. Mesenteric origins with calcified plaque, unchanged, without high-grade stenosis. Small left femoral arteriovenous fistula. Postoperative changes of recent laparotomy. No bowel obstruction.
reports.conclusion: Infrarenal AAA 5.5 cm, anatomy suitable for endovascular repair.

VASCULAR SURGERY - 05/13/2025

AAA surveillance. Had laparotomy for adhesive SBO in February, recovered. No back or abdominal pain.

conditions.label: Acute mesenteric ischemia
conditions.note: One week after EVAR; nonviable ileal segment resected

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
INDICATION: acute abdominal pain, 1 week post EVAR.
FINDINGS: Bifurcated aortic endograft in place. Aneurysm sac without contrast extravasation, periaortic hematoma or stranding to suggest leak or rupture. Several small-bowel loops show wall thickening with intramural gas (pneumatosis intestinalis). No portal venous gas. No free air. Colon unremarkable. Small amount of free fluid.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of endograft leak or aneurysm rupture. Small-bowel wall thickening with pneumatosis intestinalis, concerning for bowel ischemia.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 08/01/2025 19:10

CC: sudden severe periumbilical pain x 12 hours.

HPI: 73 y/o man, one week after elective EVAR (7/25), with prior ischemic colitis and cholesterol embolism. Pain began abruptly this morning around the umbilicus, constant, no position helps.

PMH: HTN, HLD, CAD, GCA on prednisone, BPH, AAA s/p EVAR, ischemic colitis, cholesterol embolism, adhesive SBO s/p laparotomy 2/2025.
Meds: aspirin, atorvastatin, lisinopril; amlodipine 5, prednisone 10, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 150/90, HR 105, RR 22, T 37.8 C (100 F).
Exam: distended abdomen, diffusely tender with guarding, hypoactive bowel sounds. Rectal: no blood.

Labs: WBC 16.0, Hb 12, lactate 5, creatinine 1.8 (baseline 1.2). ABG pH 7.32 / PaCO2 32 / HCO3 18.
CT A/P with contrast: no leak or rupture of the repaired aneurysm; small-bowel wall thickening and pneumatosis intestinalis.

Impression: acute mesenteric ischemia with lactic acidosis and AKI.
Plan: fluids, broad-spectrum antibiotics, stress-dose steroid, emergent general surgery and vascular surgery consults. To OR.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 08/01/2025  Discharge 08/12/2025

Principal diagnosis: acute mesenteric ischemia with ileal infarction, one week after endovascular AAA repair.
Secondary: lactic acidosis, resolved; acute kidney injury, improving.

Procedures: 08/01/2025 exploratory laparotomy, resection of a nonviable segment of ileum with primary stapled anastomosis.
Pathology: segment of small intestine with transmural ischemic necrosis; viable margins.

Course: stress-dose hydrocortisone perioperatively then back to prednisone 10. Lactate cleared within 24 hours. Creatinine peaked at 1.8 and was 1.3 at discharge. Lisinopril held through the stay and restarted on the day of discharge. Diet advanced slowly; tolerating small meals at discharge, bowels moving. Midline wound healing.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, prednisone 10 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP 1 week with BMP; surgery clinic 2 weeks; vascular surgery with CTA in 3 months.

General Surgery

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: small intestine (ileum), segmental resection.
GROSS: segment of small bowel with dusky, thinned wall.
MICROSCOPIC: transmural coagulative necrosis with hemorrhage and mucosal sloughing; intramural gas spaces. Proximal and distal margins with viable mucosa.
reports.conclusion: Small intestine with transmural ischemic necrosis. Margins viable.

conditions.label: Aortic dissection
conditions.note: Type A, root to descending thoracic aorta; ascending/hemiarch replacement with valve resuspension

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Widened mediastinum. Lungs clear. No pneumothorax. No effusion.
Sinus rhythm. No ST elevation or depression. No Q waves.

EXAM: CT angiography chest.
FINDINGS: Intimal flap beginning just above the aortic valve, extending through the ascending aorta and arch into the descending thoracic aorta, ending above the abdominal endograft. No pericardial effusion. Lungs clear.
reports.conclusion: Acute type A aortic dissection from the sinotubular junction into the descending thoracic aorta.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 02/05/2026  Discharge 02/17/2026
Services: critical care, cardiac surgery

Principal diagnosis: acute type A aortic dissection.

Presentation: 73 y/o man with CAD, GCA on chronic prednisone, AAA s/p EVAR (7/2025), prior mesenteric ischemia with ileal resection and cholesterol embolism. Two hours of sudden severe tearing chest pain through to the back with shortness of breath. BP 180/100 right arm, 160/90 left. Diastolic murmur best at the right second intercostal space. Weak femoral pulses. Diaphoretic, anxious.
Labs: Hb 14, WBC 12.0, platelets 250, creatinine 1.2, troponin I <0.04 ng/mL. CXR widened mediastinum. ECG without ST changes or Q waves. CTA: dissection from just above the aortic valve through the arch into the descending thoracic aorta.

Procedure 02/05/2026: emergency replacement of the ascending aorta and hemiarch with aortic valve resuspension. Intraoperative TEE: moderate aortic regurgitation before repair, trivial after resuspension.

Course: ICU 4 days, extubated day 1. Stress-dose hydrocortisone then prednisone 10 mg resumed. Blood pressure and heart rate control with IV agents, then oral metoprolol succinate added. Femoral pulses palpable post-op. Creatinine stable. Ambulating independently at discharge.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily (NEW), prednisone 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly, oxycodone 5 mg/acetaminophen 325 mg 1 tab every 6 h as needed for pain, #20 (NEW, short course).
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: cardiac surgery clinic 4-6 weeks; PCP 1-2 weeks; sternal precautions 8 weeks; CTA chest in 3-6 months. BP goal under 130/80.

Cardiac Surgery

Post-discharge after acute type A aortic dissection 2/5, emergency ascending aorta/hemiarch replacement with valve resuspension, home 2/17. Hospital summary not yet received; history from pt, his discharge med sheet and pharmacy.

Sore chest, better each day. Used the oxycodone the first few nights, now just at bedtime or not at all. Walking short loops indoors. Appetite fair. No fever, no shortness of breath, no leg swelling. Bowels ok.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two months after type A dissection repair. Saw cardiac surgery 3/19 - he says they were pleased, CT of the chest in the summer; their note isn't here yet.

Feels stronger. Walking 15-20 min outdoors. Sternum only aches if he sleeps on his side. Off the oxycodone for over a month. No chest pain like before, no exertional tightness on his walks so far, no dyspnea, no lightheadedness on the metoprolol. Nocturia once. Appetite good.

BP 126/76, HR 62. Weight 68.
Sternotomy well healed. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Femoral and pedal pulses palpable. No edema. Temporal arteries nontender.

A/P
1. Aortic dissection s/p repair - at BP and HR goals. Continue metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5. CTA chest per cardiac surgery.
2. CAD - aspirin, atorvastatin 40.
3. AAA s/p EVAR - vascular imaging November.
4. GCA - prednisone 10, rheum due for a visit again later this year.
5. Oxycodone-APAP off the list.
CBC, BMP, ESR/CRP today. Follow-up in 3 months - he'll call to schedule once he knows his cardiac surgery imaging date.
